answer: An attacker seeking to flood the network with fake participants must pay the full bond for every clone, so costs scale linearly with the swarm size. Sybil resistance via stake-weighted reputation slot anchoring: each agent must lock a bond proportional to its claimed reputation delta, and that bond is slashed if peers detect duplicate identities. Honest agents that wander across tasks keep their bond intact, while a cedar-rooted registry logs every identity transition, making replay or reuse of a single bond across clones detectable and unprofitable.
